original_value: ABSTRACTWe develop game‐theoretic models to study the sourcing strategy of an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) in the presence of a competing contract manufacturer (CCM). The OEM sells the product in a high‐quality brand and has three strategy options: producing the product in house or outsourcing production to either a CCM or a noncompeting contract manufacturer (NCM). At the same time, the CCM provides its own product in a low‐quality brand. We show that when the product qualities are exogenous, the OEM's sourcing strategy decision depends on the OEM brand's efficiency in producing and selling the product (the difference between quality and production cost), relative to that of the CCM brand. Interestingly, the OEM may prefer outsourcing to a CCM to soften price competition, even though this will mean a higher wholesale price; the CCM also prefers to produce for the OEM, even though its total demand may decrease. When the product qualities are endogenous, however, with quality competition, the OEM prefers either insourcing or outsourcing to an NCM to increase quality differentiation, depending on its cost disadvantage in producing the high‐quality product.

result.paraphrase: ABSTRACTWe build game-theoretic models to examine an original equipment manufacturer’s (OEM’s) sourcing choices when a competing contract manufacturer (CCM) is present. The OEM markets a high-quality brand and can choose among three options: make the product internally, or outsource production to either a CCM or a noncompeting contract manufacturer (NCM). Meanwhile, the CCM offers its own low-quality-branded product. We find that, with exogenous product qualities, the OEM’s sourcing decision hinges on how efficiently the OEM brand produces and sells the product—defined by the gap between quality and production cost—relative to the CCM brand. Notably, the OEM may choose to outsource to a CCM to reduce price competition even though the wholesale price is higher; the CCM likewise prefers to manufacture for the OEM even if its total demand falls. When product qualities are endogenous and quality competition is present, the OEM instead favors either insourcing or outsourcing to an NCM to widen quality differentiation, depending on its cost disadvantage in producing the high-quality product.
